presentingComplaint: Progressive pain, swelling and morning stiffness of the hands and wrists for 4 months.
history: A 46-year-old woman presents with a 4-month history of symmetrical pain and swelling affecting the metacarpophalangeal joints, proximal interphalangeal joints and wrists of both hands, with more recent involvement of the feet (metatarsophalangeal joints). She reports early-morning stiffness lasting over an hour that eases with activity, associated fatigue and low-grade malaise. No preceding diarrhoea, urethritis, psoriasis, photosensitive rash, oral ulcers or Raynaud's. No back stiffness. Non-smoker; mother has rheumatoid arthritis. No recent tick bite, travel or high fever.
examination: Symmetrical soft, boggy synovitis of bilateral MCPs (positive MCP squeeze), PCPs and wrists with reduced grip; MTP squeeze tender. Distal interphalangeal joints spared. No tophi, no psoriatic nail/skin changes, no dactylitis, no enthesitis. No rash, no oral ulcers, no lymphadenopathy or organomegaly. No firm subcutaneous nodules yet. Systemically well and afebrile.
imaging: Plain radiographs of hands/feet: periarticular osteopenia and early juxta-articular soft-tissue swelling; a few small marginal erosions at MCP and MTP heads. Musculoskeletal ultrasound confirms synovial hypertrophy with power-Doppler signal in wrists and MCPs.
differentialDiagnoses: SLE / other connective tissue disease arthritis
finalDiagnosis: Seropositive rheumatoid arthritis (erosive, ACR/EULAR criteria met)
citations: ACR/EULAR Classification Criteria for Rheumatoid Arthritis 2010
contraindications: Methotrexate contraindicated in pregnancy and significant hepatic/renal impairment or heavy alcohol use; check pregnancy status and baseline LFTs/FBC
NSAIDs cautioned in renal impairment, peptic ulcer disease and cardiovascular risk
Screen for latent TB and hepatitis B/C before any biologic/DMARD escalation
edgeCases: Seronegative RA (RF/anti-CCP negative) still occurs and does not exclude the diagnosis
Palindromic onset or single-joint presentation may precede established polyarthritis
Beware overlap syndromes and RA mimics such as chikungunya (recent epidemic exposure) and parvovirus B19 producing a self-limiting symmetrical polyarthritis
expectedMaiK: The symmetrical small-joint polyarthritis with prolonged morning stiffness, positive RF and high-titre anti-CCP, raised inflammatory markers and early marginal erosions is a textbook presentation of rheumatoid arthritis. Early referral to rheumatology and prompt DMARD initiation (methotrexate first-line) within the treat-to-target window limits irreversible joint damage.
expectedNextQuestions: Duration and pattern of morning stiffness and which joints are involved symmetrically?
Any psoriasis, rash, oral ulcers, recent viral illness/travel or family history of autoimmune disease?
expectedInvestigations: Plain radiographs of hands and feet (and/or joint ultrasound) for erosions

investigations: Radiographs of hands and feet / joint ultrasound
